lines.text: Every tool you use sees a sliver of your work. So you spend your best attention re-explaining context that already exists.
One workspace, one memory. Continuum already knows where you are — and decides your next step.
It finds the best resource and shows you why. It maps what you know — and when you get something wrong, the path adapts.
This is the live scholarly graph. Follow the citations, keep the paper — it lands beside your Zotero library, PDFs indexed and searchable.
Your notes don't have to move in. Continuum meets them in Obsidian — plain markdown, synced.
Everything becomes memory, retrieved by relevance — not by scrolling back.
It connects to the tools you already use —
— so the assistant is already briefed: your mastery, your weak spots, your deadline. It proposes. You approve.
And because Continuum speaks MCP, that memory follows you into Claude itself. Nothing explained twice.
Information is abundant. Learning is fragmented. Continuum is one workspace — where knowledge compounds.
